note: Monday 07:02 SGT run — BEFORE the US Monday open (~21:30 SGT) and Asia's open (SGX 09:00, HKEX 09:30), after the Fri 31 Jul US close; commentary framed 'as of the Fri US close / pre-Asia-open', sweeping Sat 1 Aug & Sun 2 Aug. Markets were shut all weekend so no new equity session has printed since Sunday's run — the tape levels stand. Fresh threads this run: (1) China's July official manufacturing PMI printed in contraction (~49.2, released ~1 Aug), keeping H2-stimulus hopes alive as Q2 GDP sits at a 3.5-yr-low ~4.3%; (2) Energy Fuels (UUUU) started building a commercial-scale HEAVY rare-earth plant at White Mesa on 29 Jul — a direct catalyst for the ex-China basket; (3) the metals pullback and hike-biased-Fed threads carry from the weekend (gold ~$4,054, silver ~$57.7, 10Y ~4.75%); (4) the 1 Aug Hormuz LNG-tanker strike keeps oil bid and the US-Iran pause broken. 5 of 14 items are dated 1-2 Aug (last 24-48h). Every item source-verified; the 1-Aug US reciprocal-tariff-deadline outcome could NOT be cleanly verified for 2026 and is omitted rather than published with a guessed detail.

items.headline: Qatari-LNG tanker struck transiting the Strait of Hormuz on 1 Aug; oil firms, US-Iran pause stays broken
items.summary: A Qatari-LNG carrier was struck by a projectile and disabled while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on 1 Aug, with a second tanker reporting a projectile splash nearby; Iran's Revolutionary Guard separately claimed it stopped two vessels attempting to exit and turned four others back (independently unconfirmed). The strait is effectively closed to commercial traffic (~4-10 transits vs ~88/day normal). Oil rose on the news after a week in which prices had fallen more than 5% on de-escalation hopes — WTI settled ~$84.67 and Brent ~$90.12 on Friday. Mediators have floated a 10-day ceasefire, but Iran's Foreign Ministry denies agreeing.
items.actionable: The Hormuz strike re-arms the oil/inflation premium that pressures the rate-sensitive book (levered silver, S-REITs, HK tech) while the Fed stays hawkish, but it restores the geopolitical safe-haven bid under gold/silver and lifts the small energy long. Keep gold-heavy GDX as the hedge against the pause staying broken; watch whether the 10-day ceasefire proposal holds when oil reopens Sunday evening and Asia opens Monday — the Hormuz front is again the key cross-portfolio swing factor.

items.headline: Gold slips ~1.5% to ~$4,054 and silver ~2.2% to ~$57.7 as hot PCE lifts the USD to a 3-week high
items.summary: The metals came off their highs into the weekend: Friday's hot-but-in-line core-PCE (+3.3% y/y) and stronger personal-spending data cut September rate-cut odds and pushed the USD (DXY ~99.8) to a 3-week high, sending gold down ~1.5% to ~$4,054/oz and silver ~2.2% to ~$57.7/oz. Both remain near record / multi-year ground and the structural silver-deficit thesis (Silver Institute 6th straight annual deficit) is intact; gold funds took their largest weekly inflow since April. Physical metals and the miners (GDX/SILJ/SLVP/SLV) are shut until Monday, so Friday's levels stand into the new week.
items.actionable: The pullback is USD/real-rate-driven, not a thesis break — but it shows the two-sided pull: a hotter Fed path (10Y ~4.75%, hike-biased September odds) is the near-term headwind for levered silver even as the Hormuz risk and sticky inflation underpin the metals. Silver's ~2.2% drop vs gold's ~1.5% is the higher-beta tell: favor gold-heavy GDX over pure silver leverage and hedge the silver-vs-gold spread rather than adding leverage into a hot-PCE, strong-dollar tape.

items.headline: China's July manufacturing PMI stays in contraction (~49.2) as Q2 GDP cools to a 3.5-yr-low ~4.3%
items.summary: China's official July manufacturing PMI printed in contraction at ~49.2 with soft new orders, keeping the factory sector below the 50 boom-bust line, while Q2 GDP cooled to ~4.3% y/y — the weakest in about 3.5 years and below the ~5% full-year target. Beijing has responded with targeted, incremental easing (service-sector interest subsidies across ~8 industries) rather than a broad stimulus, after the late-July Politburo signalled H2 support. The PBOC is expected to hold the Loan Prime Rate unchanged (1-yr 3.0%, 5-yr 3.5%) for a 14th straight month.
items.actionable: A soft PMI keeps the pressure on Beijing for more stimulus — a modest support for the HK-tech core (Tencent/Xiaomi) and the China-inflow trade — but a 14th-month LPR hold shows the easing stays incremental, not a bazooka, so the H2-stimulus bid remains a hope trade until delivered. Watch whether the Monday A-share/HK open and Tencent's 12 Aug print carry the late-July China-inflow momentum or fade it.

items.headline: Crypto stays soft over the weekend: Bitcoin ~$62.8k, Ether ~$1,920, sentiment in 'Fear' (F&G 27)
items.summary: Crypto stayed soft through the weekend after the late-July correction: Bitcoin held ~$62,800 (below its 20-day MA, stuck in a descending channel) after rejection near the top of its range, Ether eased to ~$1,900-1,920 (holding support better than BTC) and Solana ~$73, while the crypto Fear & Greed index sat at 27 ('Fear', vs 26 a week ago and 21 a month ago). Flows tilted BTC→ETH: spot-Bitcoin ETFs saw net weekly OUTFLOWS while Ether ETFs extended an inflow streak. With ETFs shut over the weekend the institutional bid is paused, leaving thinner crypto-native liquidity prone to sharper swings around the Hormuz headlines.
items.actionable: No direct holding, but crypto is the cleanest read on the risk-appetite impulse — its failure to break higher despite the equity records flags that the rate backdrop is capping risk. Treat it as a barometer: a further hawkish repricing into September would pressure both crypto and the metals/REIT rate-sensitivity trade; a dovish July-jobs surprise (7 Aug) would relieve both. Watch for weekend-liquidity air-pockets around the Hormuz headlines.

items.headline: PBOC weekend meeting: LPR seen unchanged a 14th month; Beijing leans on targeted, not broad, easing
items.summary: China's central bank held its monthly policy meeting over the weekend with the Loan Prime Rate broadly expected to stay unchanged (1-yr 3.0%, 5-yr 3.5%) for a 14th straight month, and no RRR cut anticipated. The backdrop is softening — Q2 GDP ~4.3% y/y (a 3.5-yr low) and a sub-50 manufacturing PMI — keeping expectations of additional H2 stimulus alive after the late-July Politburo signals, but Beijing continues to favour targeted measures (service-sector subsidies) over a broad bazooka. No concrete new easing was announced this weekend.
items.actionable: The stimulus-hope backdrop is a modest support for the HK-tech core and the China-inflow trade, but a 14th-month LPR hold with GDP at a 3.5-yr low shows Beijing is still incremental — the H2-stimulus bid stays a hope trade until delivered. Southbound Stock Connect has already rotated hardware→internet (favoring Tencent over SMIC/Xiaomi); watch the Monday HK open and Tencent's 12 Aug results.

items.headline: Stocks close July at records: S&P +0.7% to 7,489.72, Nasdaq +1.0%, Dow's 4th straight winning month
items.summary: US equities capped a volatile July at record highs on Friday, extending Thursday's relief rally. The S&P 500 rose 0.7% to a record 7,489.72, the Nasdaq gained 1.0% to 25,373.85 and the Dow added ~277 points (+0.53%) to 52,485.03 — all three posted weekly gains and the Dow logged a fourth straight winning month. Amazon jumped ~15% on its AWS blowout and the four megacap hyperscalers now guide to a combined $720-745bn of 2026 capital spending, re-validating the AI-infrastructure thesis. The VIX collapsed to 15.99 as equity fear drained.
items.actionable: The AI-capex-doubt scare that had pressured the SMIC/HK-tech chip leg fully reversed — a relief for the tech-beta parts of the book. But the S&P at a fresh record with the 10Y at a one-year-high ~4.75% and September a live hike risk leaves little valuation cushion, and CNN's internal breadth gauges still read Fear. Don't chase the record; keep the USD cash pile as dry powder and let this week's SGX/HK earnings and the July jobs report confirm the risk-on turn before redeploying.

items.headline: 10Y at ~4.75%, a one-year high; September Fed-hike odds stay elevated after hot PCE
items.summary: The bond market diverged sharply from the equity rally: the 10-year Treasury yield rose to ~4.75%, its highest in over a year, and the 2-year sat at ~4.28% as sticky June core PCE (+3.3% y/y) and Chair Warsh's hawkish-hold framing kept higher-for-longer intact. After Friday's hot PCE/spending data, rate markets stayed biased toward a 25bp September hike — CME FedWatch reads range widely (some ~60-65%, other feeds higher toward ~80%) but agree the path is HIKE-biased, not a cut, after three FOMC dissents favored an immediate hike at the 29 Jul meeting. Year-end projections nudged up to ~3.8%.
items.actionable: The one-year-high 10Y and a hike-biased September are the direct higher-for-longer headwind for levered silver and SGX REITs, and a warning for the most rate-sensitive parts of the book — though sticky inflation also supports SGX bank NIMs. Hedge the rate-sensitive sleeve rather than adding leverage into it; the productive USD cash pile earns ~3.5-3.75% as dry powder into Friday's July jobs report (7 Aug).

items.headline: Amazon jumps ~15% on AWS +37% blowout; four hyperscalers now guide to $720-745B 2026 capex
items.summary: Amazon rose ~15% after a Q2 beat led by AWS, which grew 37% year-over-year to $42.23B — its fastest in 18 quarters and well above the ~31% consensus — with AI and custom-chip units each running above a $25B run-rate; the company raised its 2026 capex plan to ~$220B. Combined with Microsoft, Alphabet and Meta, the four hyperscalers now guide to $720-745B of cumulative 2026 capital spending, directly reversing the AI-overcapacity narrative that had wiped >$1trn from semis the prior week. Apple was the lone soft spot, -7% on a Services/China miss.
items.actionable: The AWS +37% blowout and the $720-745bn hyperscaler capex guide re-validate the AI-infrastructure spend that the semis rout had doubted — a positive read-through to the SMIC chip leg and the whole AI-hardware complex. It argues the internet/platform layer AND the chip layer both benefit when hyperscaler capex re-accelerates; keep Tencent/Xiaomi favored but the acute bear case on the chip leg has eased.

items.headline: Q2 GDP slows to +1.5%, core PCE sticky at +3.3% — 'stagflation-lite' keeps the Fed hawkish
items.summary: The advance Q2 GDP print came in at +1.5% annualized, down from +2.1% in Q1 and below expectations — a clear growth slowdown. June headline PCE rose +3.7% y/y and core PCE stayed sticky at +3.3% y/y (in line, prior 3.4%), well above the 2% target, with hot personal spending. The combination validated the three July FOMC hike dissents and Chair Warsh's hawkish framing, sending the 10Y toward 4.75% and the 2Y to fresh 2026 highs even as equities rallied to records.
items.actionable: Sticky 3.3% core PCE keeps September a live hike risk — the direct higher-for-longer headwind for levered silver and SGX REITs, with the 10Y at a one-year high. The sub-trend growth read is a warning for the most cyclical, rate-sensitive parts of the book. Keep the big USD cash pile (~3.5-3.75%) as productive dry powder and hedge the rate-sensitive sleeve rather than adding leverage into it.

items.headline: Energy Fuels (UUUU) starts building a commercial-scale HEAVY rare-earth plant at White Mesa, Utah
items.summary: Energy Fuels announced on 29 Jul it has begun constructing a commercial-scale heavy rare-earth element (HREE) separation plant at its White Mesa mill in Utah — targeting terbium, dysprosium, samarium, europium and gadolinium oxides, with Tb/Dy circuits slated by end-2027 — a roughly $100M+ expansion, largely grant/loan-funded, moving the company toward a mine-to-magnet Western supply chain. It lands as China's heavy-REE exports remain ~50% below pre-control levels despite the one-year suspension (to Nov 2026), and alongside DoD-backed Western build-outs (Lynas's Seadrift, Texas plant).
items.actionable: A direct, dated catalyst for the ex-China rare-earth watchlist — heavy REEs (Tb/Dy) are the China chokepoint, so a Western commercial HREE plant is the structural bull case made concrete. Reinforces accumulating government-backed UUUU and MP on weakness into the 10 Nov MOFCOM suspension cliff rather than chasing; the insider open-market buying at UUUU (CEO/director, early July) validates the $12.70-13.08 reference band.

items.headline: Semis rebound with the tape but Burry adds to his Micron short (disclosed 24 Jul)
items.summary: Semiconductors bounced alongside the AWS/MSFT-led rally after a >$1trn drawdown since 24 Jul, with SMIC's HK line and the broad SOX recovering. But Michael Burry — now publishing on Substack after deregistering Scion — disclosed on 24 Jul that he ADDED to his Micron short, part of an expanded NVDA/MU/SOXX/TSLA/PLTR/CAT bear book arguing the SOX sits near the top of its 15-year forward-P/E band. Separately he trimmed (did not cover) his Palantir short with the stock in the $112-118 range. Tepper (Q1 13F) and Congress's Newhouse remain on the memory-bull side; MU was WSB's lone bearish top ticker on 2 Aug.
items.actionable: The AWS/hyperscaler capex re-validation eases the acute bear case on the SMIC chip leg near-term, but Burry's fresh, larger Micron short is the standing warning that the group is richly valued into any capex wobble. Continue favoring the internet/consumer HK names (Tencent, Xiaomi) as the core while treating the chip leg as higher-beta and two-sided; size for volatility.

items.headline: SGX banks at record highs into earnings; DBS reports 6 Aug, STI at all-time highs
items.summary: Singapore's big banks (DBS, OCBC, UOB) hit record highs in July and the STI printed all-time highs (+21% total return YTD), led by wealth-management income (DBS FY25 wealth income ~S$5.70B). Earnings season is underway: CapitaLand Ascendas REIT reports 5 Aug, DBS 6 Aug, and OCBC/UOB 7 Aug. SG banks have been upgraded to Overweight by several houses on resilient NIMs and capital returns, while the S-REIT sleeve navigates the higher-for-longer rate backdrop; SGX's own fund-flow tracker shows institutions net-selling into retail buying (a distribution pattern) at the record levels.
items.actionable: A constructive backdrop for the SGX banks/REIT sleeve into next week's prints, but the hawkish Fed (10Y ~4.75%) and the oil-spike inflation risk are fresh headwinds for the rate-sensitive S-REITs, and institutional net-selling into retail buying argues against adding to the sleeve here. Watch DBS results 6 Aug and CapLand Ascendas REIT 5 Aug; the banks are the more insulated (higher-for-longer NIM) leg vs the REITs.

items.headline: China rare-earth enforcement tightens; MP/USAR on control list, 10 Nov MOFCOM suspension cliff nears
items.summary: China's rare-earth grip tightened: MOFCOM Announcement No. 26 (a reporting-and-reward enforcement regime) took effect 1 Jul, and export curbs were extended to 14 EU firms on 24 Jul, while MP Materials and USA Rare Earth remain on China's entity-specific dual-use control list (added 22 Jun). The broad October-2025 MOFCOM export controls stay SUSPENDED only until 10 Nov 2026 (~3 months out), and heavy-REE exports remain ~50% below pre-control levels. Lynas has advanced ex-China heavy-REE production and DoD-backed Western supply continues to build.
items.actionable: Structural Western-supply validation for the ex-China rare-earth watchlist (Lynas heavy-REE, MP's DoD backing, UUUU's new HREE plant), but the 10 Nov MOFCOM suspension cliff is the calendar catalyst: near-term pricing urgency stays eased, so accumulate MP/UUUU on weakness into a potential control snap-back rather than chase the strategic re-rate now.

items.headline: Tencent pauses buyback into results blackout ahead of 12 Aug interim earnings
items.summary: Tencent ran near-daily buybacks through early July (e.g. ~1.065M shares/HK$500.7M on 9 Jul) under its 10% AGM mandate, then PAUSED the program into the customary blackout ahead of its 12 August interim results. Separately, an HKEXnews notice dated 6 Jul showed Tencent disposing of ~272.9M Kuaishou (1024) shares, ceasing to be a substantial shareholder (a capital-recycling move, not a read on its own franchise). Xiaomi's own buyback continued earlier in July.
items.actionable: The buyback blackout temporarily lifts a mechanical support under Tencent into its 12 Aug print — a reason not to add aggressively before results, even as the internet sleeve stays the preferred HK-tech core over the SMIC chip leg. Southbound flows have rotated toward Tencent and away from SMIC/Xiaomi. Watch the 12 Aug earnings (buyback resumes after) as the next catalyst.
